title: The Great Merge
space: the student's own repo `{user}/challenge-repo` (a seeded fork of the shared lab repo); its `main` is theirs alone
goal: Two feature branches, `feature-a` and `feature-b`, both edit the same lines. A third commit on one of them broke something. Bring both changes into `main` through a pull request with **both** edits kept, no conflict markers left behind, and the broken commit undone the safe way.
seed: the two conflicting branches and the bad commit are created in the student's own `{user}/challenge-repo` (Forgejo user repos, so no branch names need a `{user}` suffix).
verify_text: forgejo `pr_merged` into that repo's `main`; `file_contains` both edits and no `<<<<<<<`; history contains a revert commit for the bad one.
isolation: the merge lands in a private repo, so it can't conflict with anyone. Fully solo; no facilitator.
hints: Merge one, then the other; expect a conflict.
`git revert` undoes a commit without rewriting history.
